The Daytona Beach Road Racing Course. Florida. c. 1940

The Daytona Beach Road Course in Florida was a race track between 1902 and 1958 that was instrumental in the formation of the National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing, or NASCAR. The original lap length was 3.2 miles (5.1 km), one half on a paved road and the other right on the beach beside the Atlantic Ocean.

It originally became famous as the location where fifteen world land speed records were set. For example, in 1927 Major Henry Segrave and his Sunbeam 1000 hp Mystery set a world land speed record of 203.79 mph (327.97 km/h), becoming the first car to reach a speed over 200 mph (320 km/h).

A new 2.5-mile (4.0 km) superspeedway had been built by 1956 to host the new premiere event of the NASCAR series – the Daytona 500. Until 1961, during Daytona Speed Week, races continued on the original site but only on the beach sand and not the adjoining road,
